description: WE ARE STUDENTS of  GEC PALAKKAD Mech E
summary:
An interactive 14-Sol lunar and Martian outpost mission trainer built for young learners and STEM classrooms. Players balance real-time solar power across Life Support (ECLSS), Active Radiation Shielding, Hydroponics Bio-Dome, and ISRU Maintenance while responding to space weather alerts, radiation spikes, and crew health trade-offs grounded in NASA and CSA open science data.
Key Features:
Dual-Site Simulation: Command Shackleton Rim Outpost (Moon — cosmic radiation, crater shadow dips, water-ice mining) or Jezero Delta Station (Mars — global dust attenuation, 14–22 min comms delay, closed-loop farming) across Cadet and Commander difficulties.
Interactive Habitat Telemetry Canvas: Live animated outpost showing solar tracking, rotating ECLSS scrubbers, active proton-deflecting radiation shields, Bio-Dome LED crops, ISRU drills, surface rover patrol, and clickable module focus controls.
Strategic Planning HUD: Live resource meters (HP, O₂, BAT, FOOD, H₂O, DOSE) with educational interpretation tooltips, a 3-Sol Space Weather & Power Forecast strip, Sol-by-Sol telemetry sparklines, and a filterable Outpost Operations Log (All, Critical, Decisions, Flavor).
Mission Pacing & Audio Feedback: Procedural orbital ambient music, authentic NASA Quindar (2524 Hz / 2475 Hz) achievement chimes, mission badges/medals, 5-Sol milestone banners, and a 1-second Sol transition overlay.
NASA Data Lab: In-app scientific reference modal connecting gameplay trade-off
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Outpost Command: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive 14-Sol lunar and Martian habitat simulator designed to teach young learners how real off-world survival systems depend on one another.

Players choose between two authentic mission environments—Moon · Shackleton Crater (high cosmic radiation, solar particle storms, crater rim shadows, and abundant water-ice) or Mars · Jezero Crater (dust accumulation on solar panels, global dust storms, and 14–22 minute Earth communication delays)—and train across Cadet (Guided) or Commander (NASA Margins) difficulty.

Each Sol, players allocate finite solar and RTG kilowatts (kW) across four core subsystems via interactive sliders or by clicking directly on the animated habitat canvas:

  • Life Support (ECLSS): CO₂ scrubbing and O₂ electrolysis.
  • Radiation Shielding: Active magnetic and hydrogen-rich water-wall baffling (plus an emergency Storm Shelter mode during flares).
  • Hydroponics Bio-Dome: LED crop growth that produces fresh food, recycles O₂, and boosts crew morale.
  • ISRU & Maintenance: Ice-water mining and clearing dust off solar arrays.

Players plan ahead using a 3-Sol Space Weather & Power Forecast, inspect educational tooltips on all six telemetry meters (HP, O₂, BAT, FOOD, H₂O, DOSE), resolve real-science mission dilemmas, track trends via Sol-by-Sol charts, and review mission updates in a filterable Operations Log (All, Critical, Decisions, Flavor).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Turns Abstract STEM Into Hands-On Cause & Effect: Instead of memorizing isolated facts about oxygen or radiation, students immediately see how diverting power to survive an X2.8 solar flare reduces crop yields or drains battery reserves.
  • Built for Classrooms & Self-Guided Learning: Guided tooltips explain safe vs. critical telemetry thresholds in plain language, while 5-Sol milestone popups, 6 unlockable achievements, and tiered Mission Badges encourage replayability and experimentation.
  • Real Space Science Literacy: The built-in NASA Data Lab connects every gameplay rule to NASA DONKI solar flares, NASA RadLab / MSL-RAD radiation benchmarks, NASA OSDR human-health studies, CSA hydroponic research, and Mars Trek surface conditions.

Creativity & Design Craft

  • Living Habitat Telemetry Canvas: Features sun-tracking solar wings, spinning ECLSS turbines, active proton-deflecting shields, swaying Bio-Dome plants, ISRU drill sparks, orbiting telemetry satellites, walking crew members, and a patrolling surface rover.
  • Sensory Time & Audio Design: A 1-second Sol Transition overlay with analog grain texture and subtle screen-shake marks each day's passage. Background orbital music adapts dynamically during solar storms, and unlocking achievements triggers authentic Apollo-era NASA Quindar tones (2524 Hz / 2475 Hz) synthesized completely in code.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript, React 19, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS v4
  • Build & Runtime Tooling: Vite, Node.js, Lucide Icons
  • Graphics & Audio: HTML5 2D Canvas API (requestAnimationFrame), Web Audio API (zero external audio asset dependencies)
  • Verification & Testing: Automated simulation, forecasting, tooltip, achievement, and audio unit tests (node:test + tsx), TypeScript static checking (tsc --noEmit), and headless Chromium UI verification

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Scientific Fidelity vs. Accessibility: Real orbital/surface radiation (0.67 mSv/day on Mars vs. 1.37 mSv/day unshielded on the Moon) and power trade-offs were balanced so Cadet mode stays approachable for younger learners while Commander mode challenges advanced students.
  • Zero-Dependency Reliability: Audio synthesis and core NASA/CSA reference data work out-of-the-box offline with deterministic fallback benchmarks, so classrooms and judges never hit broken external media or API lockouts.
  • Inclusive, Responsive UX: Designed for both desktop and mobile viewports with non-color-only status indicators, keyboard shortcuts (B, P, M, Space), and reduced-motion safeguards.
